---
title: "Framing: what is \"AI\" here?"
---

## What the tool actually is

A large language model predicts text. A *coding agent* wraps that model in a loop: it
reads files, proposes edits, runs commands, reads the output, and tries again. Three
consequences follow, and they explain everything else on this site.

1. **It has no memory of your project** beyond what it reads this session. That is why
   an instruction file ([Agents](04-agents.qmd)) matters more than clever prompting.
2. **It optimizes for a plausible answer**, not a correct one. It will invent a
   variable name, a function argument, or a citation with complete fluency.
3. **It acts on your files.** Which is fine — if every change is visible and
   reversible ([Git workflow](03-git.qmd)).

## Software engineering vs. research code

Agents arrived from software engineering, where they are genuinely strong. Research code
is a different problem.

| | Software | Research code |
|---|---|---|
| Where the spec lives | Written down; tests encode it | A codebook, a literature, your judgment |
| How failure appears | Loud — it crashes or a test goes red | **Silent** — it runs and prints a number |
| Cost of a subtle error | A bug report | A published claim |
| Agent performance | Strong | Confidently wrong |

::: {.warn}
[The core asymmetry]{.warn-head}
A wrong recode does not throw an error. `pid7 == 8` is "not sure" in this survey, not
"strong Republican" — code it as the latter and your partisanship measure is quietly
wrong, every model after it is wrong, and nothing in your console will say so.
:::

## What to delegate, and what never to trust unchecked

::: {.note}
[Delegate freely]{.note-head}
Scaffolding and boilerplate · refactoring you can read · documentation · tests ·
debugging an error message · "explain what this script does" · translating Stata to R ·
the fiddly `ggplot2` call you do not want to look up.
:::

::: {.warn}
[Never accept unchecked]{.warn-head}
Variable coding and reverse-coding · which cases were dropped · weights and survey
design · anything that cites a number · anything that cites a source.
:::

## Where the tools differ

- **Copilot** is strongest at the *next line*: inline completion while you type, and
  quick questions about an open file.
- **Claude Code** (and Codex, Cursor's agent mode, Copilot agent mode) is strongest at
  the *next task*: "add income terciles to the recode, rerun it, and show me what
  changed." It edits several files and runs commands.
- **A chat window** with no repository access is the weakest option for this work: it
  cannot see your data, so it guesses your variable names.

Use the first two together. That is what we set up next.

::: {.turn}
[Discussion]{.turn-head}
Name one task in your own current project you would hand to an agent today, and one you
would not. What distinguishes them?
:::
